headline: 20+ injured as mob attacks police to reach child murder suspect in Lalmonirhat
summary: The violence erupted after a child was found dead in Aditmari Upazila, leading to the vandalism of seven government vehicles, including the DC's car.
details: At least 20 people, including the Lalmonirhat district police chief (SP) and an Officer-in-Charge (OC), were injured during clashes with an unruly mob in Folimari village of Bhelabari Union.
The violence broke out on Tuesday afternoon after a child was found dead in Aditmari Upazila, sparking outrage among local residents.
An angry crowd attacked police officers who were attempting to protect a suspect in the child's death from being lynched by the mob.
During the chaos, the attackers vandalised at least seven government vehicles, including the car designated for the Deputy Commissioner (DC) of the district.
Police used sound grenades to disperse the crowd and restore order after the clashes lasted for approximately three hours.
According to reports, some journalists were also among the injured during the unrest.
caption:
A child's death sparked a violent riot in Lalmonirhat, leaving the district police chief and 19 others injured.

At least 20 people, including the Lalmonirhat district police chief (SP) and an Officer-in-Charge (OC), were injured during clashes with an unruly mob in Folimari village of Bhelabari Union.

The violence broke out on Tuesday afternoon after a child was found dead in Aditmari Upazila, sparking outrage among local residents.

An angry crowd attacked police officers who were attempting to protect a suspect in the child's death from being lynched by the mob.

During the chaos, the attackers vandalised at least seven government vehicles, including the car designated for the Deputy Commissioner (DC) of the district.

Police used sound grenades to disperse the crowd and restore order after the clashes lasted for approximately three hours.

According to reports, some journalists were also among the injured during the unrest.

headline: Local government elections may begin from September or October
summary: Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir says polls for Union councils, municipalities, and city corporations are planned within a year.
details: Local Government Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir informed parliament on Tuesday that local government elections in Bangladesh may begin in phases starting from September or October.
The minister stated that the government plans to complete elections for Union councils, municipalities, Upazila Parishads, Zila Parishads, and city corporations within a single year.
He noted that Union council elections are likely to be held first, followed by other elections in phases, although a final schedule has not yet been confirmed.
Minister Fakhrul explained that the exact timeline and sequencing of the polls will depend heavily on budget availability and financial allocations.
The plan includes elections for 13 city corporations, including the newly formed Bogura City Corporation, within the same timeframe.
Additionally, the minister mentioned that Tk 600,000 has been allocated for each Upazila council to build inspection rooms for MPs and senior officials.
Regarding water supply, the minister told parliament that Dhaka North and South city corporations require 3.2 to 3.25 billion litres of water daily.
He added that the production capacity of Dhaka WASA stands at 2.95 to 3 billion litres, with water quality being ensured through regular testing following WHO guidelines.
caption:
Local government elections in Bangladesh could start as early as September!

Local Government Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir informed parliament on Tuesday that local government elections in Bangladesh may begin in phases starting from September or October.

The minister stated that the government plans to complete elections for Union councils, municipalities, Upazila Parishads, Zila Parishads, and city corporations within a single year.

He noted that Union council elections are likely to be held first, followed by other elections in phases, although a final schedule has not yet been confirmed.

Minister Fakhrul explained that the exact timeline and sequencing of the polls will depend heavily on budget availability and financial allocations.

The plan includes elections for 13 city corporations, including the newly formed Bogura City Corporation, within the same timeframe.

Additionally, the minister mentioned that Tk 600,000 has been allocated for each Upazila council to build inspection rooms for MPs and senior officials.

Regarding water supply, the minister told parliament that Dhaka North and South city corporations require 3.2 to 3.25 billion litres of water daily.

He added that the production capacity of Dhaka WASA stands at 2.95 to 3 billion litres, with water quality being ensured through regular testing following WHO guidelines.
